quotes.text: The raven urged Ash to hide the harvest: “Tomorrow this stranger may never find you.”
The Moon Heron rang the lantern bell. “Neither shore can force trust,” she said.
She placed half the shoots in the returning boat and planted the rest beside the bridge.
Ash divided the harvest: seven and a half seeds for the stranger, seven and a half for the reeds that sheltered the bridge.
It knew the difference between a blurred count and a closed hand.
“Why risk your supper?” asked the mountain.

note: Repeated raven-tempts, keeper returns half, fog blurs, heron rings bell template; no sanction.

quotes.text: A fox whispered that he might never meet Mara again and could keep everything.
A raven called, “Keep everything. Tomorrow the river may pair you with someone new.”
He sent half the shoots back, planting the rest beside the crossing.
Mira filled the returning boat with half the harvest.
Mist could blur numbers, never kindness.
A raven urged her to keep them all, saying the fog would hide what she had done.

note: Mara/Ivo crossings; raven/fox tempt hoarding each round, keeper returns half; fog judged patiently; no sanction.

quotes.text: the raven urged him to return nothing.
“One ring honors the courage of sending,” she said. “The other honors the care of returning.”
The Moon Heron rang its bell twice. “The first sound is for the courage to give; the second is for the care to answer.”
“Mist changes what eyes can count,” it said, “but not the courage it took to send.”
The keeper heard the fox whisper, “No one will know if you keep them all.”
“Why do the roots favor neither shore?” asked the raven.

note: Seven Springs ferryman; raven/fox tempt, keeper shares; bell-rings-twice refrain; no sanction.

quotes.text: A fox urged the keeper to close his gate and keep them all.
She returned half the harvest, trusting the stranger to carry the story onward.
“Mist bends light, not every heart. Look beyond one uncertain glimmer.”
“You could have kept everything,” said the River Spirit.
“If you owned the boat tomorrow, what shore would you hope to find?”

note: Two lanterns Trust and Return; keeper returns half; fox/raven tempts, heron counters; no sanction.

quotes.text: A shadow whispered to the keeper, “Keep the whole harvest. Strangers cannot demand a share.”
Mara divided the harvest into two equal baskets.
do not mistake a wavering shadow for a neighbor’s heart.
The fox beside her asked, “Why give anything away? Tomorrow brings another stranger.”

note: River of Threefold; fox/shadow/raven tempt keeping, rejected; equal division; no sanction.

quotes.text: a raven whisper, “Keep the harvest; the fog will hide your hand.”
She divided the harvest evenly, sending one basket home and burying the other near her lantern.
never mistake a blurred reflection for a crooked heart.
“No one can see what you keep,” it croaked.
Why share with someone you may never meet again?”

note: Moon Heron bridge; raven/fox tempt hoarding under fog; keeper divides evenly; no sanction.

quotes.text: A raven whispered, “Keep them all; tomorrow belongs to strangers.”
The raven urged the keeper to bury everything, but she returned seven and planted eight beside the landing.
The keeper chose seven seeds for the returning boat and planted eight beside the bridge.
Judge the open hand before you judge its shadow.
heard the raven croak, “They cannot see what you keep.”
“Why give away what you could hold?” she asked.

note: Moon Tree ferryman; 7-of-15 return repeated; raven tempts, flood washes away hoard; no sanction.

quotes.text: A raven offered him a plan: “Keep them all and call the mist your excuse.”
Instead he sent half the harvest back
“Mist can blur a number, but not a generous heart.”
A raven whispered, “Keep the harvest. Nobody can see your hands.”
A raven called from the bridge, “Why not keep everything? He cannot tell what you received.”

note: Bridge of Two Full Baskets / Trust Valley; raven tempts each round, keeper shares half; no sanction.
Also shared: Moon Heron's bell rung twice (courage to send, care to answer), 'Trust Valley', raven tempter; no sanction anywhere.
